## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷantaraduka* ("Shorter Intermediate Set of Dyads") is a section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final treatise of the Theravāda *Abhidhamma Piṭaka*. In the formal structure of the Abhidhamma matrix (*mātikā*), the *cūḷantaraduka* comprises a set of seven dyads covering various pairs of factors (such as conditioned and unconditioned states), functioning alongside the *mahantaraduka* and *piṭṭhiduka* as intermediate dyadic groupings distinct from the corruption-oriented clusters (*gocchaka*) [Potter 1996].

Secondary literature does not treat this section of the *Paṭṭhāna* independently; references to the *cūḷantaraduka* in modern scholarship instead address the dyad matrix as it appears in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the *Dhātukathā*, and comparative Abhidhamma taxonomy [Potter 1996].

**Sources**

- [Potter 1996] Karl H. Potter, Encyclopedia of Indian Philosophies, Vol. 7: Abhidharma Buddhism to 150 AD (1996) — Structural classification and definition of the cūḷantaraduka as the shorter intermediate set of seven dyads in the Abhidhamma matrix.
